## Foundations & Reading

- [Why Is It So Hard to Do My Work?](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.obhdp.2009.04.002) - Shows unresolved task switches leave attention residue, so finishing one item beats starting five.
- [On the Need for Attention-Aware Systems](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chb.2005.12.009) - Defines interruption cost across performance, errors, and mood, giving a baseline for any notification policy.
- [Cognitive Load During Problem Solving](https://doi.org/10.1016/0364-0213%2888%2990023-7) - Separates intrinsic, extraneous, and germane load, so redundant presentation can be deleted instead of shortened.
- [The Concept of Information Overload](https://doi.org/10.1080/01972240490507974) - Maps four decades of overload research into causes and outcomes, replacing a stack of papers with one framework.
- [Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction](https://doi.org/10.1145/3290605.3300233) - Gives 18 testable rules for when an AI should speak, so most proactive messages never get sent.
- [Humans and Automation](https://doi.org/10.1518/001872097778543886) - Distinguishes automation use, misuse, disuse, and abuse, clarifying which tasks deserve human attention at all.
- [Persuasive Computers](https://doi.org/10.1145/274644.274677) - Names captology and its functional triad, letting a designer audit a product for persuasion before shipping it.
- [The Attention Economy and the Net](https://doi.org/10.5210/fm.v2i4.519) - Frames attention as the scarce resource of networked markets, the premise behind every triage decision below.
- [The Attention Economy](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/attention-economy) - Treats attention as a design constraint and shows where interfaces spend it with no return.
- [Charts of the Week: Attention is All You Need](https://www.a16z.news/p/charts-of-the-week-attention-is-all) - Puts a ceiling on weekly media consumption, so an attention budget can be sized against real capacity.
- [Is Google Making Us Stupid?](https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/2008/07/is-google-making-us-stupid/306868) - Traces how skim-shaped media weakens sustained reading, arguing for formats that reward depth.
- [Attention economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_economy) - Summarizes the concept and its critics on one page, replacing a shelf of introductory reading.
- [如何在信息过载时代开启「独立思考」的人生](https://sspai.com/post/82646) - Turns reading from collecting into judging through a question, decompose, synthesize loop.
- [开篇语：你的注意力去哪儿了？](https://sspai.com/prime/story/vol012-opening-words) - Explains attention as a budget before recommending tools, so readers skip tool-hopping.
- [Designing Organizations for an Information-Rich World](https://gwern.net/doc/design/1971-simon.pdf) - Defines information abundance as attention poverty, the premise every later source assumes.
- [The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two](https://psychclassics.yorku.ca/Miller) - Caps working memory at a handful of chunks, so any list longer than that leaks.
- [The Computer for the 21st Century](https://doi.org/10.1038/scientificamerican0991-94) - Puts computing into the environment so interaction stops demanding foreground attention.
- [Information Foraging](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-295X.106.4.643) - Models reading as following information scent, explaining when a link or heading earns a click.
- [Augmenting Long-term Memory](http://augmentingcognition.com/ltm.html) - Uses spaced repetition to keep knowledge retrievable, replacing repeated searching with recall.
- [Information overload](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_overload) - Summarizes causes, measures, and remedies on one page, giving a fast map of the field.
- [何为「注意力经济」](https://www.aisixiang.com/data/182419.html) - Explains how platforms convert user time into revenue, naming the extraction chain.

## Awesome Lists & Meta

- [skills.sh](https://skills.sh) - Ranks installable agent skills by usage, so discovery replaces building from scratch.
- [ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills) - Indexes skills by task, cutting search time before an agent is extended.
- [Vercel skills CLI](https://vercel.com/changelog/introducing-skills-the-open-agent-skills-ecosystem) - Installs a skill with one command instead of a manual setup read-through.
- [e2b-dev/awesome-ai-agents](https://github.com/e2b-dev/awesome-ai-agents) - Indexes agents by task, so delegating work starts from a candidate instead of a blank page.
- [Meirtz/Awesome-Context-Engineering](https://github.com/Meirtz/Awesome-Context-Engineering) - Collects context-engineering papers and tools, reducing trial and error on what to feed a model.
- [hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code](https://github.com/hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code) - Curates Claude Code workflows and commands, so proven automation replaces manual reading and editing.
- [plenaryapp/awesome-rss-feeds](https://github.com/plenaryapp/awesome-rss-feeds) - Supplies curated feeds and OPML, replacing an algorithmic timeline with chosen subscriptions.
- [anthropics/claude-plugins-official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official) - Lists official plugins, so a workflow is installed instead of assembled from documentation.

## Distill: Docs to Answers

- [anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) - Ships docx, pdf, pptx, and xlsx skills that extract the answer from a document instead of requiring a full read.
- [MCP reference servers](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers) - Moves fetch, memory, and structured reasoning out of the prompt, so context holds conclusions rather than raw pages.
- [Exa MCP](https://exa.ai/mcp) - Returns extracted page content from one semantic query, replacing a browse, click, and scrape loop.
- [Context7](https://github.com/upstash/context7) - Pulls version-matched library docs on demand, ending the retry cycle caused by stale examples.
- [mcp-summarization-functions](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-summarization-functions) - Summarizes commands, files, and directories before they enter context, cutting a long dump to its decision points.
- [读者用 AI“代读”公众号，转发的人反而更多了](http://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=Mzg5NDg2NjY1NQ==&mid=2247484990&idx=1&sn=b5477a19ae90cf941f44d86434961fdd) - Separates filtering from understanding, showing where AI reading saves time and where it loses the point.
- [mozilla/readability](https://github.com/mozilla/readability) - Extracts article text and drops ads and sidebars, so one page yields only the paragraph that matters.
- [trafilatura](https://github.com/adbar/trafilatura) - Extracts main text in bulk, cutting a crawl of noisy pages down to readable content.
- [Full-Text RSS](https://fivefilters.org/content-only) - Serves the article body from a feed link, removing the page visit and its surrounding clutter.
- [summarize](https://github.com/steipete/summarize) - Condenses a URL or video into key points before a reader commits time to it.
- [docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) - Converts documents into structured data, so a PDF becomes searchable and answerable instead of skimmed.
- [marker](https://github.com/datalab-to/marker) - Converts PDFs to clean Markdown at high accuracy, making a long report queryable in one pass.
- [firecrawl-mcp-server](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server) - Fetches a page as Markdown for an agent, replacing a browse and copy cycle.
- [简悦 SimpRead](https://github.com/Kenshin/simpread) - Strips page chrome into a clean reading view, removing the scan past navigation and ads.
- [DeepWiki MCP](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/deepwiki-mcp) - Answers questions about a public repository with cited wiki content, so a person skips cloning and reading the source.

## Triage: Rank, Dedupe, Batch

- [Effects of Intelligent Notification Management](https://doi.org/10.1145/1357054.1357070) - Delaying notifications to task boundaries sharply reduces disruption, so batching beats instant delivery.
- [An In-Situ Study of Mobile Phone Notifications](https://doi.org/10.1145/2628363.2628364) - Measures about 63.5 notifications a day, most rated low value, setting a realistic cut line.
- [Indicators, Validations, and Notifications](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/indicators-validations-notifications) - Splits messages into three classes, so most feedback becomes inline status instead of a notification.
- [Five Mistakes in Designing Mobile Push Notifications](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/push-notification) - Shows how permission-first and blast pushes train users to ignore alerts, and what to send instead.
- [@yonki/dedup](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@yonki/dedup) - Detects duplicate and near-duplicate files before they are read twice.
- [Info-Pigu 信息辟谷](https://github.com/bluelava/infopigu) - Deduplicates pages by claim and shows only the cognitive increment, removing repeated reading.
- [apprise](https://github.com/caronc/apprise) - Funnels many notification sources into one gateway, so a person checks one channel instead of eight.
- [Notification settings on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/iph7c3d96bab/ios) - Groups and schedules alerts into summaries, moving most pings out of the current moment.
- [Notification Cooldown](https://www.androidauthority.com/android-16-notification-cooldown-3501276/) - Suppresses repeated alerts from the same app, cutting a burst down to its first useful signal.
- [信息过载时代，我的漏斗式阅读工作流](https://sspai.com/post/107554) - Deduplicates, summarizes, and ranks feeds before human review, so only survivors reach the reader.
- [Octobox](https://octobox.io) - Adds archive and filter states to GitHub notifications, so an inbox is cleared in batches instead of one thread at a time.

## Maps & Progressive Disclosure

- [The Coming Age of Calm Technology](https://calmtech.com/papers/coming-age-calm-technology.html) - Argues technology should move between center and periphery, so most status lives in the background.
- [Progressive Disclosure](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure) - Defers secondary controls until requested, keeping the first screen to the few choices that matter.
- [Agent Skills 官方文档](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview) - Loads only skill metadata until a trigger fires, so context carries the map, not every manual.
- [Equipping agents with Agent Skills](https://www.anthropic.com/research/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills) - Explains why metadata-first loading scales an agent without inflating every prompt.
- [Calm Technology 原则](https://calmtech.com) - States eight low-interruption principles, moving status to the periphery and keeping the center free.
- [Designing and Evaluating Glanceable Peripheral Displays](https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2007/EECS-2007-56.pdf) - Establishes how a glance can carry status without a task switch.
- [Ambient Displays](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-69706-3_4) - Shows how light and sound carry information at the edge of attention.
- [pydantic-ai-skills](https://github.com/DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills) - Loads skill metadata first and bodies on demand, keeping the prompt to the relevant slice.
- [Understand Anything](https://github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything) - Turns a codebase into a searchable knowledge graph, so orientation starts from one map instead of a file-by-file crawl.

## Calm & Focus

- [A Pace Not Dictated by Electrons](https://doi.org/10.1145/2207676.2207754) - Finds an email-free group reports lower stress and longer focus blocks, quantifying the cost of inbox checking.
- [Disconnecting Distraction](https://paulgraham.com/distraction.html) - Uses a separate machine for the internet so focus survives without willpower.
- [It's Time to Dismantle the Technopoly](https://www.newyorker.com/tech/annals-of-technology/its-time-to-dismantle-the-technopoly) - Argues for cutting tools rather than defaulting to all of them, one less feed per cut.
- [How to Thrive in the Attention Economy](https://greatergood.berkeley.edu/article/item/how_to_thrive_in_the_attention_economy) - Inserts a pause between stimulus and response, turning a reflex reply into a chosen one.
- [Your Attention Didn't Collapse. It Was Stolen](https://www.theguardian.com/science/2022/jan/02/attention-span-focus-screens-apps-smartphones-social-media) - Reframes focus loss as structural rather than personal, pointing effort at design instead of guilt.
- [我用这些方法夺回被侵占的注意力](https://sspai.com/post/59606) - Cuts interruptions at four layers: app settings, push, RSS, and shortcuts.
- [重建注意力的边界](https://sspai.com/post/110789) - Uses deliberate friction, such as Opal, to raise the cost of an impulsive app open.
- [zenfeed](https://github.com/glidea/zenfeed) - Turns a full RSS feed into a scored daily brief, replacing scrolling with one read.
- [Folo](https://github.com/RSSNext/Folo) - Aggregates subscriptions and summarizes with AI before display, so a feed is read as a brief.
- [miniflux/v2](https://github.com/miniflux/v2) - Shows a plain title list with no recommendations, ending the scroll into suggested content.
- [newsboat](https://github.com/newsboat/newsboat) - Reads feeds in a terminal with no images or algorithm, so the session ends when the list does.
- [RSSHub](https://github.com/DIYgod/RSSHub) - Turns sites without feeds into subscriptions, replacing repeated manual visits.
- [wallabag](https://github.com/wallabag/wallabag) - Strips an article to its body for later reading, removing ads and layout from the session.
- [SelfControl](https://github.com/SelfControlApp/selfcontrol) - Blocks chosen sites for a timed window, removing the choice to check them.
- [one sec](https://one-sec.app) - Forces a pause before an app opens, interrupting the automatic reach.
- [Set up a Focus on iPhone](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/set-up-a-focus-iphd6288a67f/ios) - Silences selected apps and people per context, cutting interruptions to the chosen set.
- [Digital Wellbeing](https://support.google.com/android/answer/9346420) - Caps app time and schedules focus, making overuse visible before it consumes the day.
- [changedetection.io](https://github.com/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io) - Watches a page and reports only the change, replacing repeated refresh checks.
- [为什么我们要减少阅读新闻](https://sspai.com/post/77426) - Argues news consumption is low-value and biased, justifying cutting whole sources.
- [信息断舍离：取关 70 个公众号](https://sspai.com/post/75569) - Cuts subscriptions in bulk and tolerates the empty slot, reducing homogeneous input.
- [科技爱好者周刊](https://github.com/ruanyf/weekly) - Packs a week of tech news into one curated issue, replacing daily feed checking.

## Attention-Saving Dev Workflow

- [Expectations, Outcomes, and Challenges of Modern Code Review](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICSE.2013.6606617) - Finds review value sits mostly in communication, so line-level nitpicking can be dropped.
- [Modern Code Review: A Case Study at Google](https://doi.org/10.1145/3183519.3183525) - Shows small changes and fast turnaround carry the practice, keeping each review inside a fixed attention budget.
- [The End of Code Review](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13175) - Argues coding agents can absorb mandatory review, moving human attention to specs and acceptance.
- [Best Practices for Peer Code Review](https://smartbear.com/learn/code-review/best-practices-for-peer-code-review) - Puts the effective limit at 200 to 400 lines and 60 to 90 minutes per session.
- [CodeRabbit](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/code-review-overview) - Summarizes a pull request and ranks comments by risk, so review starts at the risky hunk.
- [Graphite AI Reviews](https://graphite.com/features/ai-reviews) - Runs a machine pass before the human one, leaving only judgment calls in the queue.
- [Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/docs/introduction) - Maps a change against the whole repository, removing manual cross-file tracing.
- [serena](https://github.com/oraios/serena) - Retrieves code by symbol and reference, so an agent reads the relevant function instead of whole files.
- [repomix](https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix) - Packs a repository into one structured prompt, replacing a file-by-file read.
- [claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) - Persists context across sessions, removing the re-explanation at the start of each task.
- [i-have-adhd](https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd) - Forces the answer first and detail later, cutting the read before the conclusion.
- [DeepSeek Super-agent Prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype) - Runs a persistent router that triages incoming events and delegates to isolated workers, so a human tracks one queue instead of three to five sessions.

## Anti-Patterns & Research

- [The Cost of Interrupted Work](https://doi.org/10.1145/1357054.1357072) - Measures higher stress after interruptions even when work speeds up, pricing the "quick question".
- [No Task Left Behind?](https://doi.org/10.1145/1054972.1055017) - Finds 57 percent of work segments are interrupted, documenting how fragmented the day already is.
- [Disruption and Recovery of Computing Tasks](https://doi.org/10.1145/1240624.1240730) - Records recovery time and switch patterns after an interruption, giving a measurable cost per ping.
- [If Not Now, When?](https://doi.org/10.1145/985692.985727) - Shows interruption cost varies widely by moment, so timing alone saves attention.
- [A Diary Study of Task Switching and Interruptions](https://doi.org/10.1145/985692.985715) - Documents frequent switching and slow recovery across a real work week.
- [Alarm Fatigue: A Patient Safety Concern](https://doi.org/10.4037/NCI.0b013e3182a903f9) - Reports 72 to 99 percent of clinical alarms are false, producing desensitization and missed true alarms.
- [Alert Fatigue in Security Operations Centres](https://doi.org/10.1145/3723158) - Reviews SOC alert fatigue and its countermeasures, the operations-side version of the same failure.
- [Does Automation Bias Decision-Making?](https://doi.org/10.1006/ijhc.1999.0252) - Finds people trust automated advice enough to miss visible errors, so verification must be forced.
- [The Flaws of Policies Requiring Human Oversight](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clsr.2022.105681) - Argues human-in-the-loop review often becomes a formality, weakening rather than adding control.
- [Does the Whole Exceed Its Parts?](https://doi.org/10.1145/3411764.3445717) - Shows AI explanations can increase over-reliance, so explanation design must prevent attention laziness.
- [IM, Not IP](https://doi.org/10.1145/966712.966731) - Names real-time interruption as information pollution and argues for managed information instead.
- [Losing in the Attention Economy](https://stratechery.com/2026/losing-in-the-attention-economy) - Uses a stalling game industry to show that attention is a zero-sum market.
- [The Acceleration of Addictiveness](https://paulgraham.com/addiction.html) - Explains how technology compresses want into over-want, the mechanism behind compulsive checking.
- [How Technology Hijacks People's Minds](https://medium.com/@tristanharris/how-technology-hijacks-peoples-minds-from-a-magician-and-google-s-design-ethicist-56d62ef5edf3) - Lists ten hijacking patterns, giving a checklist for auditing an interface.
- [AI slop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_slop) - Defines bulk low-quality AI content, the category a feed filter must remove first.
- [2025 Word of the Year: Slop](https://www.merriam-webster.com/wordplay/word-of-the-year) - Records the term entering mainstream use, confirming slop as a named filter target.
- [We Are Hopelessly Hooked](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/2016/02/25/we-are-hopelessly-hooked) - Reviews persuasive design practice from the inside, exposing the ethics behind habit loops.
- [TikTok's Enshittification](https://doctorow.medium.com/tiktoks-enshittification-bb3f5df91979) - Traces a feed degrading from user-serving to advertiser-serving, explaining why noise rises over time.
- [How Wikipedia Is Fighting AI Slop Content](https://www.theverge.com/report/756810/wikipedia-ai-slop-policies-community-speedy-deletion) - Shows community-level fast deletion plus AI-feature checklists stopping low-quality pages early.
- [Enshittification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enshittification) - Names the three-stage platform decay pattern, so the drain is recognized before it is felt.
- [当我们的注意力成为货币](https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1924124186651099843) - Explains how platforms monetize attention and where to cut the extraction chain.
- [大脑的“硬伤”，竟然被“快餐式”AI 读书无限放大了](http://m.chinanews.com/wap/detail/cht/zw/10608985.shtml) - Shows how AI book summaries amplify existing reading biases, a limit on delegated reading.
- [Deceptive Patterns — Types](https://www.deceptive.design/types) - Classifies dark patterns with legal mappings, so a manipulative flow is named in seconds.
- [Dark Patterns at Scale](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.07032) - Audits 11,000 shopping sites and quantifies manipulative design, turning an anecdote into evidence.
- [Doomscrolling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doomscrolling) - Names compulsive negative-news scrolling, making the behavior visible enough to interrupt.

## Organization & Life

- [Getting the Attention You Need](https://hbr.org/2000/09/getting-the-attention-you-need) - Frames attention as an organizational resource split by overload and lean staffing.
- [It's Time to Embrace Slow Productivity](https://www.newyorker.com/culture/office-space/its-time-to-embrace-slow-productivity) - Replaces parallel work with a short sequential queue, removing most switch cost.
- [如何应对信息过载？](https://www.zhihu.com/question/297546899) - Collects reusable reading and filtering workflows instead of a single tool recommendation.
- [Getting Things Done](https://gettingthingsdone.com) - Moves open tasks into a trusted list, so unfinished work stops resurfacing as attention residue.
- [Inbox Zero](https://web.archive.org/web/2020/https://www.43folders.com/izero) - Processes messages in scheduled batches to empty, replacing constant inbox checks.
- [Progressive Summarization](https://fortelabs.com/blog/progressive-summarization-a-practical-technique-for-designing-discoverable-notes/) - Compresses notes in layers, so a later read starts at the summary instead of the source.
- [Deep Work](https://calnewport.com/writing) - Argues for long uninterrupted blocks, making switch cost a scheduling decision.

## Use It as a Skill
